# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/Size.sol#L87-L105


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Detailed description of the impact of this finding.

The initialise function can be called by any address, which means that any user can initialise the proxy contract with arbitrary values. This can lead to unauthorised control over the contract and potential loss of funds or misconfiguration.

## Proof of Concept
Provide direct links to all referenced code in GitHub. Add screenshots, logs, or any other relevant proof that illustrates the concept.

1. Create the following foundry test in this file path: test/local/actions/InitializeDebo.t.sol
2. Go to terminal> then go to the root folder called 2024-06-size> then run: forge test -vvvv --match-contract InitializeDeboTest
```sol
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity 0.8.23;

import {BaseTest} from "@test/BaseTest.sol";

import {ERC1967Proxy} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/proxy/ERC1967/ERC1967Proxy.sol";

import {Size} from "@src/Size.sol";

contract InitializeDeboTest is BaseTest {
  
    function test_Debo_proxy_can_be_initialized() public {
        address owner = address(this);
        Size implementation = new Size();
        vm.prank(address(0xbEEF));
        ERC1967Proxy proxy = new ERC1967Proxy(
            address(implementation), abi.encodeWithSelector(Size.initialize.selector, owner, f, r, o, d)
        );

        assertEq(Size(payable(proxy)).riskConfig().crLiquidation, 1.3e18);
    }

}
```

## Tools Used
Manual review and foundry test for POC.
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Re-configure the access control modifiers so that there is no misconfigurations that allow access to any address.


## Assessed type

Access Control
